Optional: overrides the identity as the: 選填：取代識別名稱作為代理程式註冊時使用的名稱。
Optional: overrides {{variable}} as the: 選填：取代 {{variable}} 作為代理程式註冊時使用的名稱。
Other rules still cover this severity an: Other rules still cover this severity and rule type, so deleting this one does not leave a gap.
Outbound webhook requests sent for this: Outbound webhook requests sent for this {{itemName}}.
Overlaid queries use different units ({{: Overlaid queries use different units ({{units}}) — they share one axis, so values may not be directly comparable.
Pages visited just after this one, acros: Pages visited just after this one, across every analysed session that visited it, not only this step of the map. A session counts once per page, and the percentage is of all sessions that visited this page, so sessions that left from here add nothing. The 6 most common are listed.
Pages visited just before this one, acro: Pages visited just before this one, across every analysed session that visited it, not only this step of the map. A session counts once per page, and the percentage is of all sessions that visited this page, so landings add nothing. The 6 most common are listed.
People and teams responsible for this {{: People and teams responsible for this {{resourceName}}. They are notified about changes.
Physical memory (RAM) the .NET process o: Physical memory (RAM) the .NET process occupies, called its working set. Averaged across instances in each interval; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Physical memory (RAM) the process occupi: Physical memory (RAM) the process occupies, also called resident memory. Averaged across instances in each interval; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Physical memory (RAM) this process holds: Physical memory (RAM) this process holds, called resident set size or RSS, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the range (usually the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or with no recent data). The percentage below compares it with the host's total RAM.
Physical memory (RSS) held by this proce: Physical memory (RSS) held by this process in each interval of the selected range.
Physical memory (RSS) this process held: Physical memory (RSS) this process held at its newest reading in the last 15 minutes, with its share of the host's total RAM. The bar turns amber at 10% and red at 20% of RAM.
Placement groups (the chunks Ceph splits: Placement groups (the chunks Ceph splits each pool into) by state from the last 10 minutes: clean groups have every copy in place, degraded and undersized ones are missing copies, and Other is the rest, such as peering. A group can be in several states at once, so the segments are approximate.
Placement groups, the chunks Ceph splits: Placement groups, the chunks Ceph splits each pool into, that are degraded (missing copies) or undersized (on fewer OSDs than the pool's copy count), from the last 10 minutes of data. A group in both states is counted twice.
Pods by phase in the latest inventory: R: Pods by phase in the latest inventory: Running, Succeeded (all containers finished without error, such as completed jobs), Pending (not started yet) and Failed (stopped with an error). Not tied to the time range.
Pods in the latest inventory in any phas: Pods in the latest inventory in any phase - running, pending, completed or failed - not limited to the selected range. A pod is one or more containers that run together on a node.
Pods of this StatefulSet passing their r: Pods of this StatefulSet passing their readiness checks, out of the number it is set to run (its desired replicas).
Pods of this StatefulSet passing their readiness checks, out of the number it should run. Green when all are ready, amber when only some are, red when none are.
Pods of this deployment passing their re: Pods of this deployment passing their readiness checks, out of the number it is set to run (its desired replicas).
Pods of this job that are pending or run: Pods of this job that are pending or running right now, as of the latest snapshot from your cluster.
Pods of this job that ended in failure,: Pods of this job that ended in failure, counting every retry. Once failures go past the backoff limit, Kubernetes stops retrying and marks the job as failed.
Pods of this job that have finished succ: Pods of this job that have finished successfully. When the job sets a completions count, it is done once this reaches that count.
Pods placed on a node with at least one: Pods placed on a node with at least one container running, starting or restarting. Running does not mean healthy - a container can still be failing its readiness check.
Pods that have stayed ready for at least: Pods that have stayed ready for at least the deployment's minimum ready time (minReadySeconds, 0 unless set), so they count as available to serve.
Pods the cluster has accepted but not st: Pods the cluster has accepted but not started yet - usually waiting for a node with enough free CPU or memory, for an image to download, or for a volume. Any pending pod marks the cluster Degraded.
Pods whose containers have all stopped,: Pods whose containers have all stopped, with at least one ending in an error; they will not be restarted. Any failed pod, even one left behind by a finished job, marks the cluster Unhealthy.
Ports on this device from its last succe: Ports on this device from its last successful SNMP walk: up means enabled with a working link, down means enabled with no link. Ports an administrator switched off count in neither and fill the grey rest of the bar.
Ports that are enabled but have no link,: Ports that are enabled but have no link, summed over all devices from each device's last successful SNMP walk. A switch with three dead ports adds three to this number.
Post an update to your status page…: Post an update to your status page…
Powered on, Powered off or Template, inf: Powered on, Powered off or Template, inferred from whether the VM sent CPU data in the latest collection, so a suspended VM shows as Powered off. A dash means the VM has not been collected yet.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in the clu: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in the cluster, as counted by vCenter itself at its latest report.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this cl: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this cluster, as counted by vCenter itself at the latest report.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this vC: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this vCenter, templates excluded, from the latest inventory. Only the total is shown until the agent has reported power state.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs, templates: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs, templates excluded, from the latest inventory; a VM that is off is not treated as a fault. Power state is inferred from which VMs send CPU data, so a suspended VM counts as off.
Processes and threads running inside all: Processes and threads running inside all containers on this host, added together and averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). Each thread counts as one.
Processes and threads running inside eac: Processes and threads running inside each container, averaged per interval. A count that keeps climbing can point to a leak or a runaway process.
Processes running or ready to run on a C: Processes running or ready to run on a CPU in the newest interval; the total on the line below counts every state and is updated at most about once a minute. Where states are not reported, as on Windows, it counts every process seen in the last 5 minutes.
Projected monthly change in cost if this: Projected monthly change in cost if this container's recommendation is applied, scaled from the selected range to a 730-hour month. Green is a saving; amber with + is the extra cost of giving it enough.
Proxmox does not report an uptime for st: Proxmox does not report an uptime for storage volumes, so this column normally shows a dash.
RAM in use across all ESXi hosts in each: RAM in use across all ESXi hosts in each interval of the selected range, as a share of their combined RAM.
RAM in use on each host against its tota: RAM in use on each host against its total RAM, with a bar for the share in use, from its latest report. N/A when the host has sent no data in the last 15 minutes.
Read and write operations per second (IO: Read and write operations per second (IOPS) from clients, added up across all pools. Worked out for each interval of the selected time range from Ceph's running per-pool operation counters.
Read and write operations per second (IOPS) on this pool, worked out for each interval of the selected time range from Ceph's running operation counters.
Readiness for {{name}} was not checked -: 未檢查 {{name}} 的就緒狀態——此策略的回應者數量超出了就緒檢查的範圍，因此此標記顯示為未知而不是就緒。完整清單請開啟「回應者就緒狀態」卡片。
Recorded sessions from this person that: Recorded sessions from this person that started in the selected range. The line below shows how many are still live (not yet closed off, which can take a few minutes after the visitor leaves), or else when their earliest session in the range started - not necessarily their first visit ever.
Recorded sessions that started in the pa: Recorded sessions that started in the past 24 hours; the server can reuse its answer for up to 30 seconds. Playable is every session except those closed with no footage or whose recording was lost, so sessions still recording count as playable. The newest start can be older than 24 hours.
Recorded time across these sessions, add: Recorded time across these sessions, added up. Each runs from its start to its last recorded moment, idle time included; one still recording counts what it has so far. The line below counts page changes made inside the app without a full reload; a page opened by a full load is not counted.
Refresh this page after a few minutes —: Refresh this page after a few minutes — the {{resourceNoun}} switches to Connected once its first data arrives.
Repeating is on, but the number of repea: Repeating is on, but the number of repeats is set to {{count}}, so the policy still runs only once. Set a repeat count to have it try again.
Replay upload bytes let through since 00: Replay upload bytes let through since 00:00 UTC for the whole project, all applications together, as the recorders sent them (usually compressed). The percentage is of this deployment's daily limit: amber from 80%, and at 100% recorders are told to stop until the next UTC day.
Replay upload bytes this application sen: Replay upload bytes this application sent since the 1st of the month (UTC), against its own monthly budget: amber from 80%, stopped at 100%. Only counted while a budget is set, so with none it reads 0, and bytes sent before a budget was set are not included.
Resident set size (RSS): the physical me: Resident set size (RSS): the physical memory (RAM) the Python process occupies. Averaged across instances in each interval; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Round-trip time from the probe to this h: Round-trip time from the probe to this hop and back, from the first reply the hop sent. Routers often answer slowly, so one high hop matters less than a jump that carries on to the hops after it.
Route did not reach the destination.

Run the {{cli}} run command from the set: Run the {{cli}} run command from the setup guide on this host. Set {{variable}} as below so the data lands on this {{resourceNoun}}:
Running guests (virtual machines and con: Running guests (virtual machines and containers) out of all guests, from the latest report. The net figure is their combined traffic in and out per second over the last 5 minutes of the selected range, often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data.
Running or Stopped, as Proxmox last repo: Running or Stopped, as Proxmox last reported for each guest. A stopped guest is not an error unless it is set to start on boot.
Running or Stopped, as Proxmox last reported for this guest. A stopped guest only counts against cluster health when it is set to start on boot.
Running tasks out of the tasks this serv: Running tasks out of the tasks this service wants, such as 2/3, from the latest inventory snapshot. Green when every wanted task is running; amber when some are missing or the service is scaled to 0.
Running tasks, replicas or instances in: Running tasks, replicas or instances in this environment that sent telemetry in the last 15 minutes. It is a live count, so it ignores the selected time range.
Running tasks, replicas or instances tha: Running tasks, replicas or instances that sent telemetry in the last 15 minutes, across every cloud environment in this project, archived ones included.
Running, Powered off or Template: the sa: Running, Powered off or Template: the same inferred power state as the Power State column, shown as a colored label you can filter on.
Save this as docker-compose.yml in a dir: 將此內容儲存為 docker-compose.yml，放在{{noun}}上的專屬目錄中，與 .env 檔案並列。
Save this as docker-compose.yml in {{dir: 將此內容儲存為 docker-compose.yml，放在{{noun}}上的 {{directory}} 中，與 .env 檔案並列。
Services defined in the swarm at the age: Services defined in the swarm at the agent's latest inventory snapshot, whatever their state, including ones scaled to 0. The cluster's overview shows how many have every wanted copy running.
Services defined in this swarm - each te: Services defined in this swarm - each tells Swarm which image to run and how many copies to keep running. Converged counts the services with every wanted copy running; a service scaled to 0 never counts as converged.
Session Replay recordings that started i: Session Replay recordings that started in the selected range and match the Sessions and Device filters; one whose pages are all hidden drops out. At most the newest 5,000 recordings are read, so on a busy range the line below says how many there were in total.
Sessions at this step with an error reco: Sessions at this step with an error recorded on this page, on this visit or another: an uncaught JavaScript error, an unhandled promise rejection or a failed file load. The line below counts frustration signals (rage, dead and error clicks, repeated reloads) the same way. Both are placed on pages as in the Pages table.
Sessions that left one of these pages fo: Sessions that left one of these pages for the other and came straight back, counted once per session however often they went round; the bar and percentage are their share of all analysed sessions. The 10 most common pairs are listed.
Sessions that recorded an error while on: Sessions that recorded an error while on this page: an uncaught JavaScript error, an unhandled promise rejection or a file that failed to load. An error is placed on the page the visitor was on when its recording chunk was sent, so one just before moving on can land on the next page.
Sessions that went straight from the fir: Sessions that went straight from the first page to the second at these two steps of the map. The same move made at another step is counted on that step's band instead, and a band touching Other pages covers several pages folded together.
Sessions that were on this page at this: Sessions that were on this page at this step of the map, each counted once. The line below is their share of every session with a page at this step, whichever page it was.
Sessions whose first recorded page was t: Sessions whose first recorded page was this one, at this step before the chosen page: they arrived on the application here. The line below is their share of this step's sessions on the page. On the map's last step, sessions that came from further back are not counted.
Sessions whose last recorded page was th: Sessions whose last recorded page was this one, at this step: the visitor left, or the recording stopped, here. The line below is their share of this step's sessions on the page, red from 50%. On the map's last step, sessions that went on further are not counted.
Sessions with a frustration signal on th: Sessions with a frustration signal on this page: a rage click (3 or more clicks within a second in one spot), a dead click (something that looks clickable did nothing for 3 seconds), an error within a second of a click, or the same page loaded 3 or more times in a minute. Placed on pages the same way as Errors.
Set up broker metrics for this queue →: Set up broker metrics for this queue →
已向 {{name}} 傳送設定提醒。
Share of CPU time across all cores spent: Share of CPU time across all cores spent running programs and the operating system, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the range. 100% means every core was busy; on ranges over 12 hours or with no recent data, it is usually the whole-range average.
Share of CPU time spent running programs: Share of CPU time spent running programs and the operating system (user plus system time), averaged across all cores, in each interval of the selected range. 100% means every core was busy for the whole interval.
Share of each host's CPU capacity in use: Share of each host's CPU capacity in use, from its latest report. N/A when the host has sent no data in the last 15 minutes.
Share of its available CPU the process u: Share of its available CPU the process used (100% means all of its CPUs were busy); if your SDK splits CPU time by mode (user, system) this averages those values rather than adding them, so it reads lower than total use. As a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Share of samples in the selected range i: Share of samples in the selected range in which the unit was Active (a service running, a socket listening, a timer waiting to fire); Reloading counts as not active. Only the newest 2,000 samples count, and the tile says capped when there are more.
Share of status samples in the selected: Share of status samples in the selected range in which the service was Running; samples usually arrive every 30 seconds. Only the newest 2,000 samples count, and the tile says capped when the range holds more.
Share of the VM's configured virtual CPU: Share of the VM's configured virtual CPU capacity in use, from its latest report; N/A when nothing arrived in the last 15 minutes. CPU is only reported while a VM is on, so a powered-off VM may show its last reading.
Share of the cluster's raw disk space in: Share of the cluster's raw disk space in use, counting every copy of your data, from its latest data. The bar turns amber at 75% and red at 90%.

Share of the cluster's raw disk space in use, counting every copy of your data, from the latest readings rather than the chart time range. The subtitle projects the last 24 hours' growth to 85%, Ceph's default nearfull warning level.
Share of the combined CPU capacity of al: Share of the combined CPU capacity of all ESXi hosts in use, with bigger hosts counting for more. Averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data); the chart below covers the whole range.
Share of the combined RAM of all ESXi ho: Share of the combined RAM of all ESXi hosts in use, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). The line below shows used and total RAM at the latest point.
Share of the host's physical memory (RAM: Share of the host's physical memory (RAM) in use in each interval of the selected range, not counting file cache the system can free.

Share of the host's physical memory (RAM) in use, not counting file cache the system can free, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the range. On ranges over 12 hours, or with no recent data, it is usually the whole-range average; below is the total RAM.
Share of the last 24 hours this site spe: Share of the last 24 hours this site spent outside a non-operational status such as Degraded or Offline. Scheduled maintenance is left out, and time before the site's first health rollup counts as up.
Share of the last 30 days this site spen: Share of the last 30 days this site spent outside a non-operational status, with scheduled maintenance left out. One full day of outage lowers it by only about 3.3 points; time before the first rollup counts as up.
Share of the period in the title this si: Share of the period in the title this site spent outside a non-operational status such as Degraded or Offline, leaving out scheduled maintenance on the site or its parents. Time before the first rollup counts as up; red means below 99%.
Share of the selected range in which One: Share of the selected range in which OneUptime received metrics (a heartbeat) from this cluster's agent, leaving out the latest intervals whose data may still be arriving. It shows whether the cluster was reporting, not whether your apps were up.
Share of this VM's configured virtual CP: Share of this VM's configured virtual CPU capacity in use, with the amount in MHz or GHz, from the latest report. CPU is only reported while the VM is on, so a VM that is now off shows its last reading.
Share of time the VM was ready to run bu: Share of time the VM was ready to run but waited for a physical CPU, from its last report, however old; above about 10% busy hosts are slowing it down. A VM that is now off keeps its last reading.
Share of time this VM was ready to run b: Share of time this VM was ready to run but had to wait for a physical CPU, from its latest report (for a VM that is now off, its last reading). Above 10% it is flagged as CPU contention: the host is too busy and the VM is slowed down.
Show callers and callees of {{name}}: 顯示 {{name}} 的呼叫端與被呼叫端
Show only schedules with a coverage gap: 僅顯示本月有待命空檔的排程
僅顯示本週有待命空檔的排程
Show the {{count}} recommendations that: Show the {{count}} recommendations that are already created
Show the {{count}} recommendation that is already created
Show the {{count}} recommendations that are not set up yet
Show the {{count}} recommendation that is not set up yet
Show {{count}} kernel threads: 顯示 {{count}} 個核心執行緒
Showing the first {{shown}} of {{total}}: 按名稱顯示此團隊擁有的 {{total}} 個排程中的前 {{shown}} 個。
按名稱顯示 {{total}} 個排程中的前 {{shown}} 個。開啟某個團隊的「待命排程」頁面，即可只查看該團隊擁有的排程。
Showing the {{shown}} busiest of {{total: 顯示 {{total}} 個消費服務中最繁忙的 {{shown}} 個。
顯示 {{total}} 個發布服務中最繁忙的 {{shown}} 個。
Site link — colored by its monitor; dash: Site link — colored by its monitor; dashed when it has none
Sites directly beneath this one in the h: Sites directly beneath this one in the hierarchy, one level down. Their own child sites are not counted here.
Sites whose health, rolled up from the d: Sites whose health, rolled up from the devices at and beneath them, is non-operational, such as Degraded or Offline. Counts the whole project, whatever filters are set below.
Sites with no health status yet because: Sites with no health status yet because no device at or beneath them has reported, including sites whose last status was deleted. They are not counted as unhealthy.
Size of the .NET garbage-collected heap: Size of the .NET garbage-collected heap at the last collection. It is reported per generation (gen0, gen1, gen2, large and pinned objects) and this is the average per generation, not the total; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Some services, such as Azure Monitor act: Some services, such as Azure Monitor action groups, send a verification email before they deliver any alerts. It shows up on this monitor's Overview page like any other email.
Someone is on call for {{percent}}% of t: 該時段中有 {{percent}}% 的時間有人待命。其餘時間，路由到此排程的警示不會通知任何人。確切時間請看下方的最終排程。
Space still free on this datastore: its: Space still free on this datastore: its capacity minus the used space, from the latest report.
Space taken up on this datastore by VM d: Space taken up on this datastore by VM disks, snapshots and other files, from the latest report.
Space used compared with the volume's to: Space used compared with the volume's total size, with the percentage used, at its latest report. Shows N/A when Proxmox has not reported both numbers.
Space used on each datastore against its: Space used on each datastore against its total capacity (used plus free), with the share used, from its latest report, however old.
Space used on this mount and its total s: Space used on this mount and its total size (used, free and reserved space added up), each averaged over the selected range. Sizes use 1024-based units, so 1 GiB is 1,024 MiB.
Space used on this storage volume at its: Space used on this storage volume at its latest report.
Spans naming this queue that ended with: Spans naming this queue that ended with an error status in the selected range: failed publishes, receives, message processing and settlements alike, with their share of all its spans. A failure the client library did not record as an error is not counted.
Spans recorded for this function (matche: Spans recorded for this function (matched by its faas.name attribute) in the selected range. An invocation usually produces one span, plus more for the database and service calls it makes, so this can be higher than the true invocation count.
Spans recorded for this function in each: Spans recorded for this function in each interval, with the ones whose status was Error as a second line. One invocation can produce several spans.
Spans reported from this environment in: Spans reported from this environment in each interval, with the ones whose status was Error as a second line. Every service running in the environment counts.
Spans this service reported in each inte: Spans this service reported in each interval, with the ones whose status was Error as a second line. Every operation counts - incoming requests, database queries and outgoing calls.
Standard measures of how fast and stable: Standard measures of how fast and stable your pages feel to real visitors. Each value is an average over the selected range; Google's own report uses the 75th percentile, so its rating can differ.
Storage pools the cluster reported in it: Storage pools the cluster reported in its latest data. A pool holds data under its own replication and placement rules; block devices, file systems and object storage each keep their data in pools.
Swarm CPU and memory are collected per t: Swarm CPU and memory are collected per task container, not per node, so these columns show N/A for nodes. The Tasks list shows each task's node and what it is using.
Swarm CPU and memory are collected per task container, not per service, so these columns show N/A for services. The Tasks list names each task's service and shows what it is using.
Swarm-wide networks, such as overlay net: Swarm-wide networks, such as overlay networks and the built-in ingress network, that connect services across nodes. Networks that exist on a single node only, such as bridge or host, are not counted.
Sync attempts of this replication job th: Sync attempts of this replication job that have failed in a row since its last successful sync, as Proxmox currently reports them. Anything above zero means the copy on the target node may be out of date, and it marks the cluster at least Degraded.
Tasks Swarm wants running at the latest: Tasks Swarm wants running at the latest inventory snapshot (one task is one container of a service), shown as how many are actually running out of that total. The rest are still starting, or have stopped or failed.
Tasks Swarm wants running, where one tas: Tasks Swarm wants running, where one task is one container of a service; running counts those actually running, while the rest are starting, stopped or failed. From the latest inventory snapshot, so a replaced task can linger for up to about 25 minutes.
Teams shares a chat's name once the OneU: Teams shares a chat's name once the OneUptime app in that chat asks for the {{permission}} permission, which takes an update of the app in the chat.
Temperature in degrees Celsius from each: Temperature in degrees Celsius from each device's most recent report. A dash means the device does not report temperature.
Temperature in degrees Celsius that this: Temperature in degrees Celsius that this device reported most recently. Like the other values here, it is the last one sent, even if the device has since gone quiet.
The 1-minute load average from the newes: The 1-minute load average from the newest interval: about how many processes were running or waiting for a CPU (Linux also counts ones waiting on disk). The % divides it by the number of cores, and over 100% means work is queuing.
The 10 destination IP addresses that rec: The 10 destination IP addresses that received the most bytes in the selected range, by this device's flow records. Bytes and Packets are each address's totals.
The 10 protocol and destination port pai: The 10 protocol and destination port pairs, such as TCP 443, that carried the most bytes in the selected range. Bytes and Packets are totals for each pair.
The 10 source IP addresses that sent the: The 10 source IP addresses that sent the most bytes in the selected range, by this device's flow records. Bytes and Packets are each address's totals.
The 10 source and destination pairs that: The 10 source and destination pairs that exchanged the most bytes in the selected range, counting each direction separately. Bytes and Packets are totals for each pair.
The 5 ESXi hosts using the largest share: The 5 ESXi hosts using the largest share of their CPU capacity, from the latest inventory rather than the selected range. Hosts with no data in the last 15 minutes are left out.
The 5 ESXi hosts using the most RAM, in: The 5 ESXi hosts using the most RAM, in bytes, from the latest inventory, leaving out hosts with no data in the last 15 minutes. The bar shows the share of each host's RAM in use (or, if that is not reported, its usage compared with the top host's).
The 5 fullest datastores, by used space: The 5 fullest datastores, by used space as a share of capacity. Each value is the datastore's latest report, however old, not the selected range.
The 5 guests using the most CPU at their: The 5 guests using the most CPU at their latest report, each as a share of the CPU cores assigned to that guest. Guests that have sent no update in the last 15 minutes are left out.
The 5 guests using the most memory at th: The 5 guests using the most memory at their latest report, in bytes, with a bar for each guest's usage as a share of its assigned memory. Guests that have sent no update in the last 15 minutes are left out.
The 5 pods using the most CPU, as a shar: The 5 pods using the most CPU, as a share of the allocatable CPU of the node each runs on (what the node can hand out to pods), or in cores where that is unknown. Uses each pod's latest minute of data from the past hour and ignores the time range picker.
The 5 pods using the most memory, as a s: The 5 pods using the most memory, as a share of the allocatable memory of the node each runs on (what the node can hand out to pods), with the amount below. Uses each pod's latest minute of data from the past hour and ignores the time range picker.
The 5 powered-on VMs that spent the most: The 5 powered-on VMs that spent the most time waiting for a physical CPU (CPU Ready), from the latest inventory, leaving out VMs with no data in the last 15 minutes. Above 10% a VM is slowed by busy hosts.
The 95th percentile event duration in ea: The 95th percentile event duration in each interval: 95% of the page loads, requests and interactions in that interval finished faster than the line.
The 95th percentile page load time in ea: The 95th percentile page load time in each interval: 95% of the page loads in that interval finished faster than the line. A spike means some visitors waited much longer than usual.
The 95th percentile span duration in eac: The 95th percentile span duration in each interval: 95% of this function's spans in that interval finished faster than the line. A spike means some invocations were much slower than usual.
The 95th percentile span duration in each interval: 95% of this service's spans in that interval finished faster than the line. A rise means the slowest operations are getting slower.
The CPU and memory request the Vertical: The CPU and memory request the Vertical Pod Autoscaler recommends for this container, based on its observed usage (its target value). CPU is in cores or millicores (m); memory is in bytes or a unit such as k, Mi or Gi.
The CPU and memory this container asks K: The CPU and memory this container asks Kubernetes to set aside for it; a pod is only placed on a node with that much free. CPU is in cores, and an m suffix means thousandths of a core.
The OSD's latest apply and commit latenc: The OSD's latest apply and commit latency in milliseconds, as reported by Ceph: how long writes take to reach its disk, where values that stay high point to a slow or failing disk. Shows a dash if it has not reported in the last 15 minutes.
The Responder readiness card on this pol: 此策略概覽中的「回應者就緒狀態」卡片列出了具體是哪些以及如何修正。
The Runner only needs outbound HTTPS to: The Runner only needs outbound HTTPS to {{host}}. It does not accept inbound connections.
The VMware agent does not report when a: The VMware agent does not report when a VM was created or started, so this column is empty for every virtual machine.
The agent must still run with {{variable: The agent must still run with {{variable}}="{{hostName}}". A different name sends the data to a different {{resourceNoun}}.
The allowlist entries {{patterns}} use a: 允許清單項目 {{patterns}} 對變更所涉及的物件使用了 *，因此預先核准的是一整類變更，而非單一變更。在「自動」模式下，所有符合此形式、風險較高的變更（針對 * 涵蓋的任何物件）都會直接執行，不會詢問任何人。儘管如此，{{protections}}。
允許清單項目 {{patterns}} 對變更所涉及的物件使用了 *，因此預先核准的是一整類變更，而非單一變更。在「自動」模式下，所有符合此形式、風險較高的變更（針對 * 涵蓋的任何物件）都會直接執行，不會詢問任何人。儘管如此，{{protections}}。
允許清單項目 {{patterns}} 對變更所涉及的物件使用了 *，因此預先核准的是一整類變更，而非單一變更。此{{noun}}切換到「自動」模式後，所有符合此形式、風險較高的變更（針對 * 涵蓋的任何物件）都會直接執行，不會詢問任何人。儘管如此，{{protections}}。
允許清單項目 {{patterns}} 對變更所涉及的物件使用了 *，因此預先核准的是一整類變更，而非單一變更。此{{noun}}切換到「自動」模式後，所有符合此形式、風險較高的變更（針對 * 涵蓋的任何物件）都會直接執行，不會詢問任何人。儘管如此，{{protections}}。
The amount of storage this claim asked f: The amount of storage this claim asked for. Kubernetes binds it to a volume at least this big, so the provisioned capacity can be larger.
The average battery level of the devices: The average battery level of the devices that report one, using each device's most recent readings in the selected time range. The bar turns amber below 40% and red below 20%.
The average number of pages in a session: The average number of pages in a session's journey, with the median below: half of the sessions saw that many pages or fewer. Going back to an earlier page counts again, but a reload counts once, a return within one recording chunk (about 15 seconds) is missed, and hidden pages are left out.
The average recorded length of the sessi: The average recorded length of the sessions on this path, from the start of their first recording chunk to the end of their last, idle time included. It covers the whole session, including any pages past the 8 shown.
The average wireless signal strength of: The average wireless signal strength of the devices that report one, using each device's most recent readings in the selected time range. It is in dBm, which is negative: closer to 0 is stronger, around -50 is excellent and below -100 is weak.
The chart was added to the selected dash: The chart was added to the selected dashboard.
The chart was added to the {{dashboard}}: The chart was added to the {{dashboard}} dashboard.
This monitor gets a new random address,: 此監測器將取得一個新的隨機地址，目前的地址會立即失效。
The email address contains this monitor': The email address contains this monitor's secret key, so only people who can edit monitors can see it. Ask one of them to set it up.
The fastest and the slowest round trip a: The fastest and the slowest round trip among the pings in this test. A wide gap between the two means the delay on the path is uneven.
The fewest pods this autoscaler will sca: The fewest pods this autoscaler will scale its target down to, however quiet things get.
The first hand-off time must be at or af: 首次交接時間必須等於或晚於輪換開始時間。
The first level is notified immediately;: 第一層會立即收到通知；如無人確認，其餘各層會{{rightAway}}介入。
第一層會立即收到通知；如無人確認，警示會在 {{duration}}後升到最後一層。
第一層會立即收到通知；沒有可以繼續上報的層級。
The five pools closest to full: data sto: The five pools closest to full: data stored divided by data stored plus the space still writable (Max Avail). Max Avail allows for replication and the fullest OSDs, so a pool can fill before the cluster's raw space does.
The five pools holding the most data, by: The five pools holding the most data, by Ceph's STORED figure: what clients wrote, before replication copies. Pools that have not reported in the last 15 minutes are left out.
The guest's Proxmox high-availability (H: The guest's Proxmox high-availability (HA) state. 'started' is normal, 'error' or 'fence' means a problem, and a dash means HA does not manage the guest.
The heartbeat URL contains this monitor': The heartbeat URL contains this monitor's secret key, so only people who can edit monitors can see it. Ask one of them to set it up.
The highest CPU reading of each containe: The highest CPU reading of each container in each interval, so short spikes are not averaged away. By default only the 10 containers that peaked highest are drawn; 100% is one full CPU core.
The highest memory percentage of any con: The highest memory percentage of any container (of its memory limit, or of host memory if it has none), picked per interval and averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data).
The highest memory percentage of any container on this host in each interval of the selected range. Each container is measured against its memory limit, or against host memory if it has none.
The highest memory use of each container: The highest memory use of each container in each interval, so short spikes are not averaged away. By default only the 10 containers that peaked highest are drawn.
The highest share of the probe's regular: The highest share of the probe's regular pings that went unanswered in any one minute of the past hour. 0% means every ping in the hour got a reply.
The install command contains this monito: The install command contains this monitor's secret key, so only people who can edit monitors can see it. Ask one of them to set it up.
The kind of systemd unit, read from the: The kind of systemd unit, read from the end of its name: Service (a background program), Socket, Timer, Mount, Target and so on.
The language this service runs on, from: The language this service runs on, from the telemetry.sdk.language attribute your OpenTelemetry SDK sends, else the runtime name or the tech stack you set. Shown here because no runtime metrics (CPU, memory, heap) arrived in the selected range.
The last poll could not reach this devic: The last poll could not reach this device — neither ping nor SNMP answered.
The last poll reached this device (ping: The last poll reached this device (ping or SNMP).
The last time a recording chunk (about 1: The last time a recording chunk (about 15 seconds of footage) from this application was stored, written at most once a minute; amber after 6 hours without one. When one refusal reason has 5 or more below, this shows how many uploads were refused instead.
The last time this application contacted: The last time this application contacted OneUptime, written at most once a minute. A page fetching the Session Replay policy counts, but so does a replay upload or any other telemetry the app sends, so it can be recent even where the recorder is missing. Amber after 24 hours with nothing.
The latest CPU reading this task or inst: The latest CPU reading this task or instance sent - one snapshot, not an average - kept until a newer one arrives. Depending on the platform, 100% is one full CPU core or all the CPU the task was given, so it can read above 100%. A dash means no CPU reading has arrived.
The latest CPU use of every pod in this: The latest CPU use of every pod in this namespace added up, each as a share of its own node's allocatable CPU (what the node can hand out to pods), so it can pass 100% (the bar stops there). Only pods that reported in the last 15 minutes count.
The latest CPU use of pods from this Cro: The latest CPU use of pods from this CronJob's runs that reported in the last 15 minutes, added up, each as a share of its node's allocatable CPU (what the node can hand out to pods), so it can pass 100%. N/A between runs; same-named CronJobs in other namespaces are added in too.
The latest CPU use of this DaemonSet's p: The latest CPU use of this DaemonSet's pods (usually one per node) added up, each as a share of its own node's allocatable CPU (what the node can hand out to pods), so it can pass 100%. Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes, including same-named DaemonSets in other namespaces.
The latest CPU use of this StatefulSet's: The latest CPU use of this StatefulSet's pods added up, each as a share of its own node's allocatable CPU (what the node can hand out to pods), so it can pass 100% (the bar stops there). Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes, including same-named StatefulSets in other namespaces.
The latest CPU use of this deployment's: The latest CPU use of this deployment's pods added up, each as a share of its own node's allocatable CPU (what the node can hand out to pods), so it can pass 100% (the bar stops there). Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes, including same-named deployments in other namespaces.
The latest CPU use of this job's pods ad: The latest CPU use of this job's pods added up, each as a share of its own node's allocatable CPU (what the node can hand out to pods), so it can pass 100%. Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes (so N/A soon after the job ends), including same-named jobs in other namespaces.
The latest criteria evaluation came from: The latest criteria evaluation came from {{probe}}. Pick it above to see why it passed or failed.
The latest memory use of every pod in th: The latest memory use of every pod in this namespace added up: the total amount, and the sum of each pod's share of its node's allocatable memory (what the node can hand out to pods), which can pass 100%. Only pods that reported in the last 15 minutes count.
The latest memory use of pods from this: The latest memory use of pods from this CronJob's runs that reported in the last 15 minutes: the total amount, and the sum of each pod's share of its node's allocatable memory (what the node can hand out to pods), which can pass 100%. N/A between runs; same-named CronJobs in other namespaces are added in too.
The latest memory use of this DaemonSet': The latest memory use of this DaemonSet's pods added up: the total amount, and the sum of each pod's share of its node's allocatable memory (what the node can hand out to pods), which can pass 100%. Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes, including same-named DaemonSets in other namespaces.
The latest memory use of this StatefulSe: The latest memory use of this StatefulSet's pods added up: the total amount, and the sum of each pod's share of its node's allocatable memory (what the node can hand out to pods), which can pass 100%. Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes, including same-named StatefulSets in other namespaces.
The latest memory use of this deployment: The latest memory use of this deployment's pods added up: the total amount, and the sum of each pod's share of its node's allocatable memory (what the node can hand out to pods), which can pass 100%. Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes, including same-named deployments in other namespaces.
The latest memory use of this job's pods: The latest memory use of this job's pods added up: the total amount, and the sum of each pod's share of its node's allocatable memory (what the node can hand out to pods), which can pass 100%. Counts pods that reported in the last 15 minutes (so N/A soon after the job ends), including same-named jobs in other namespaces.
The latest memory-in-use reading this ta: The latest memory-in-use reading this task or instance sent - one snapshot, not an average or a peak - kept until a newer one arrives. For an ECS task the whole task's figure is preferred over a single container's. A dash means no memory reading has arrived.
The less visited pages this step folds i: The less visited pages this step folds into Other pages, each with the sessions that were on it at this step and their share of the sessions in Other pages. The busiest pages keep their own place, as many as Pages per step allows; at most 50 are listed here.
The link's negotiated speed in megabits: The link's negotiated speed in megabits per second, as the device reports it. This is the most the port can carry and what Utilization is measured against.
The metrics this monitor evaluates, over: The metrics this monitor evaluates, over the {{window}}.
The monitor bound to this device has not: The monitor bound to this device has not reported a status yet.
The most CPU and memory this container m: The most CPU and memory this container may use. At its CPU limit it is slowed down (throttled); if it goes over its memory limit it is killed (OOMKilled).
The most pods of this job that may run a: The most pods of this job that may run at the same time. 0 means the job is effectively paused.
The most pods this autoscaler may scale: The most pods this autoscaler may scale its target up to, however busy things get.
The most pods this node is configured to: The most pods this node is configured to run at once. It caps how many pods fit here even when CPU and memory are still free.
The name this {{noun}} reports. The agen: 此{{noun}}回報的名稱。代理程式必須以完全相同的名稱註冊，否則會服務另一個{{noun}}。
The named problems, such as OSD_DOWN or: The named problems, such as OSD_DOWN or PG_DEGRADED, that were still raised in the latest data Ceph sent in the last 10 minutes, with how serious each one is. They explain why the cluster's health is not OK.
The node is close to its limit on runnin: The node is close to its limit on running processes (PIDs). New containers may fail to start and Kubernetes may evict pods.
The node is running low on disk space fo: The node is running low on disk space for images and container data. Kubernetes may evict pods and delete unused images to free space.
The node is running low on memory. Kuber: The node is running low on memory. Kubernetes stops placing new pods on it and may evict running pods to free memory.
The page the most analysed sessions ende: The page the most analysed sessions ended on - the last page recorded before the visitor left or the recording stopped - with their share below. A high share can simply be where journeys are meant to end, such as an order confirmation.
The page the most analysed sessions star: The page the most analysed sessions started on, with their share of all analysed sessions below. Pages are compared by path without the query string; with Group IDs in URLs on, /orders/1 and /orders/2 are one page, /orders/:id.
The part of total spend charged to names: The part of total spend charged to namespaces and workloads - total spend minus idle and unallocated capacity.
The readiness answer for this policy doe: 此策略的就緒狀態檢查未涵蓋 {{names}}，因此他們顯示為未知，而不是就緒。請開啟「待命 > 就緒狀態」查看完整清單。
The restriction 'From' and 'To' times ca: The restriction 'From' and 'To' times cannot be the same. Choose a window with a positive duration (or set the restriction to None for 24/7 coverage).
The server reported \"{{outcome}}\" with: 伺服器回報了「{{outcome}}」，但沒有說明原因。
The service's state in the newest sample: The service's state in the newest sample in the selected range: Running, Stopped, Paused, or a start, stop, pause or resume still in progress. The line below says how long ago that sample was taken.
The service's status across the selected: The service's status across the selected range. Where one point on the chart covers several samples it shows the worst status among them, so a short stop stays visible.
Services that consumed from this queue i: 所選範圍內從此佇列消費的服務，依繁忙程度排序：取走的訊息數、失敗率和 p95 處理時間（p95 表示第 95 百分位數：95% 耗時更短）。
Services that published to this queue in: 所選範圍內向此佇列發布訊息的服務，依繁忙程度排序：傳送的訊息數、失敗率和 p95 發布時間（p95 表示第 95 百分位數：95% 耗時更短）。
The share of analysed sessions that saw: The share of analysed sessions that saw only one page: they never moved to another page before the recording ended. Reloading the page does not count as moving on, and hidden pages are ignored. The line below is how many sessions that is.
The share of events in the selected rang: The share of events in the selected range that were marked as errors, such as a failed page load or network request; the line below is how many errored. The bar turns amber at 1% and red at 5%.
The share of pings in this test that got: The share of pings in this test that got no reply, followed by how many replies came back out of the pings sent. Any loss on a wired link is worth investigating.
The share of sessions on this path that: The share of sessions on this path that hit at least one error anywhere in the session: an uncaught JavaScript error, an unhandled promise rejection or a file that failed to load, as the replay recorder captured them.
The share of this band's sessions for wh: The share of this band's sessions for which the page they moved to was one they had already visited earlier in the session, even before the part the map shows, such as going back to a list. Amber from 50%.
The share of this environment's spans in: The share of this environment's spans in the selected range whose status was set to Error; the line below is how many errored. The bar turns amber at 1% and red at 5%.
The share of this function's spans in th: The share of this function's spans in the selected range whose status was set to Error; the line below is how many errored. The bar turns amber at 1% and red at 5%.
The share of this service's spans in the: The share of this service's spans in the selected range whose status was set to Error by your instrumentation. The bar turns amber at 1% and red at 5%.
The status last reported by a monitor th: The status last reported by a monitor that watches this device, such as Operational or Offline. It can differ from Reachability because a monitor may also check things like ports going down; Not monitored means no monitor has reported yet.
The storage actually provisioned for thi: The storage actually provisioned for this claim, which can be more than was requested because storage providers round up. N/A until the claim is bound to a volume; Gi means gibibytes (1 Gi = 1,024 Mi).
The timeline covers {{past}} days back a: 時間軸涵蓋過去 {{past}} 天和未來 {{future}} 天。此範圍中帶陰影的部分不在該視窗內。
The top {{count}} functions account for: The top {{count}} functions account for {{share}} of the top sampled functions — those are your optimization targets.
The top {{count}} functions account for {{share}} of the window — those are your optimization targets.
The total size of this persistent volume: The total size of this persistent volume, in Kubernetes units: Gi is gibibytes and Mi is mebibytes (1 Gi = 1,024 Mi).
The total size of this storage volume at: The total size of this storage volume at its latest report.
The unit's state across the selected ran: The unit's state across the selected range. Where one point on the chart covers several samples it shows the worst state among them, so a brief failure stays visible.
The unit's state in the newest sample in: The unit's state in the newest sample in the selected range, as systemd reports it: Active, Inactive, Failed, Activating and so on. The line below says how long ago that sample was taken.
The {{collectorName}}'s docker-compose.y: {{collectorName}} 的 docker-compose.yml 已內含此服務；新安裝會直接執行它。若是較舊的安裝，請將此服務新增至 {{directory}} 中的 docker-compose.yml——它會從同一個 .env 讀取下方的所有變數。
The {{containerName}} container should b: The {{containerName}} container should be listed and Up. If it is missing or restarting, start it again from the setup guide.
The {{containerName}} container should be listed and Up. If it is missing or restarting, start it again with docker compose up -d.
There was an error while connecting with: There was an error while connecting with Microsoft Teams. Please try again.
These monitors will be created on this {: These monitors will be created on this {{resourceName}}. Everything below applies to every monitor in this batch.
These times are in the schedule's timezo: 這些時間採用排程的時區：{{timezone}}。
These times are in your local timezone:: 這些時間採用你的本地時區：{{timezone}}。
They need to add and verify a notificati: 他們需要在「使用者設定」中新增並驗證通知方式，詳情見此策略概覽中的「回應者就緒狀態」卡片。
This band's sessions as a share of every: This band's sessions as a share of every session on the page it leads to, at that step of the map: of the people there, how many came this way.
This band's sessions as a share of every session on the page it starts from, at that step of the map: of the people there, how many went this way next.
This check required {{attempts}} to comp: This check required {{attempts}} to complete and ultimately failed.
This container's most recent CPU reading: This container's most recent CPU reading as a share of the allocatable CPU on its node (what the node can hand out to pods), not of its own CPU limit. It is the latest sample, not an average; N/A means no reading in the last 15 minutes.
This container's most recent memory use,: This container's most recent memory use, shown as a share of its memory limit (the most it may use before it is killed) when it has one, up to 100%. Without a limit only the amount is shown; N/A means no reading in the last 15 minutes.
This criteria will be checked at positio: This criteria will be checked at position {{position}}.
This device has not been polled yet.
This device sent no flow records in the: This device sent no flow records in the stretch you zoomed into. Double-click here, or use Reset zoom, to go back to the time range before the zoom.
This device sent no flow records in the stretch you zoomed into. Double-click here, or use Reset zoom, to go back to the {{range}}.
This guest's state in Proxmox high avail: This guest's state in Proxmox high availability (HA), which restarts it on another node if its node fails. 'started' is normal; 'error' or 'fence' means HA hit a problem and marks the cluster Unhealthy.
This is a global override, so it applies: 這是全域覆寫，適用於每個上報到此排程的待命策略。
This is the last rule covering {{cells}}: This is the last rule covering {{cells}}. Deleting it leaves those with no rule.
This is the last rule covering {{cells}}. Deleting it leaves that with no rule.
This is the last rule that delivers for: This is the last rule that delivers for {{cells}}. The only rules left for them are opt-outs, so nothing will be sent for them once this is gone.
This is the last rule that delivers for {{cells}}. The only rule left for it is an opt-out, so nothing will be sent for it once this is gone.
This is the only escalation level on thi: 這是此策略唯一的上報層級。刪除後，此策略將沒有可通知的人，路由到這裡的事件也不會呼叫任何人。
This layer produces no on-call coverage: 此層完全不提供待命涵蓋。請在下方至少新增一名使用者，否則此層永遠不會呼叫任何人。
This looks like a {{vendor}} device — th: This looks like a {{vendor}} device — the {{template}} OID template is recommended when creating monitors.
This monitor is measured by {{count}} SL: This monitor is measured by {{count}} SLOs
This monitor is measured by {{count}} SLO
This monitor now receives email at the a: This monitor now receives email at the address below. The previous address ({{address}}) no longer works.
This monitor was created {{time}}; earli: This monitor was created {{time}}; earlier days have no data.
This monitor gets a new random address,: 此監測器將取得一個新的隨機地址，{{address}} 會立即失效。
This node's most recent CPU reading, sys: This node's most recent CPU reading, system processes included, as a share of its allocatable CPU (what is left for pods after the system's reservation), so it can pass 100%. It is the latest sample, not an average; N/A means no reading in the last 15 minutes.
This node's most recent memory use, and: This node's most recent memory use, and that as a share of its allocatable memory (what pods can use, or its total memory when allocatable is not reported). It includes file cache and the percentage stops at 100%; N/A means no reading in the last 15 minutes.
This node's state in Proxmox high availa: This node's state in Proxmox high availability (HA), the feature that restarts guests on another node when one fails. 'online' is normal and 'maintenance' is planned; 'fence' means HA is cutting the node off after a failure and marks the cluster Unhealthy.
This override is scoped to one on-call p: 此覆寫僅限於一個待命策略，因此只會改道經由該策略上報的警示。
This override is scoped to the {{policy}: 此覆寫僅限於 {{policy}} 策略，因此只會改道經由 {{policy}} 上報的警示。
This pod's most recent CPU reading as a: This pod's most recent CPU reading as a share of the allocatable CPU on its node (what the node can hand out to pods) - not of the pod's own CPU request or limit. It is the latest sample, not an average; N/A means no reading in the last 15 minutes.
This pod's most recent memory use, compa: This pod's most recent memory use, compared with the sum of the memory limits its containers set, or with its node's allocatable memory (what the node can hand out to pods) when none sets a limit. The percentage stops at 100%; N/A means no reading in the last 15 minutes.
This policy has {{total}} responders, mo: 此策略有 {{total}} 位回應者，超過此卡片一次能讀取的數量。下面的數字和清單涵蓋受影響最嚴重的 {{shown}} 位；未顯示的人排在所有已顯示的人之後。
This probe has not reported a result yet: This probe has not reported a result yet. Results usually appear within a few minutes of its next check.
This probe is disabled for this monitor,: This probe is disabled for this monitor, so it is not collecting any data. Enable it under Probes.
This process's threads, averaged over th: This process's threads, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the range (usually the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or with no recent data); open file handles are below. Both need the collector's process.threads and process.open_file_descriptors turned on.
This queue's identifier could not be rea: This queue's identifier could not be read, so no metrics can be matched to it.
This queue's identifier could not be read, so no telemetry can be matched to it.
This queue's identifier could not be read, so no traces can be matched to it.
This queue's identifier could not be read, so no {{signal}} can be matched to it.
This revokes the {{agentName}}'s key. Th: 這會撤銷 {{agentName}} 的金鑰。代理程式會在幾分鐘內自動重新註冊。如果代理程式已遷移，或其金鑰可能已外洩，請使用此功能。
This site's overall status, rolled up fr: This site's overall status, rolled up from the devices here and at every site beneath it: the worst device status by default, or a share-of-devices-down rule set in Settings. Maintenance on this site does not hide its own outage.
This step's sessions on this page as a s: This step's sessions on this page as a share of every session the map is drawn from: all analysed sessions, or with After a page or Before a page, only those that visited the chosen page.
This time is in the schedule's timezone:: 此時間採用排程的時區：{{timezone}}。
This time is in your local timezone: {{t: 此時間採用你的本地時區：{{timezone}}。
This works in the channel OneUptime crea: 這適用於 OneUptime 為此{{resourceName}}建立的頻道中的訊息和回覆。OneUptime 會在一分鐘內偵測到回應，儲存訊息，並在討論串中回覆確認。
This {{itemName}} could not be identifie: This {{itemName}} could not be identified, so it was not deleted. Please refresh and try again.
This {{resourceName}} has not sent data: 此{{resourceName}}尚未傳送資料。其代理回報後會顯示建議。
Threads in the .NET thread pool, which r: Threads in the .NET thread pool, which runs async and request work; a count that keeps climbing often means work is blocking threads. Averaged across instances; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Threads running in the Java virtual mach: Threads running in the Java virtual machine. SDKs split the count by thread state or daemon flag, and this is the average of those series rather than their total, so read it as a trend; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Time since the device last restarted, wo: Time since the device last restarted, worked out from the uptime counter it reported at its last successful SNMP walk. That counter also restarts with the SNMP agent and rolls over after about 497 days, so it can read short.
Times below are shown in the schedule's: 下面的時間按排程的時區（{{timezone}}）顯示，也就是實際呼叫所用的時區。
Times in {{timezone}}. Past shifts are r: 時間採用 {{timezone}}。過去的班次會按每個排程的目前設定重新計算。
To monitor IPv6 destinations, run the pr: To monitor IPv6 destinations, run the probe on a host that has IPv6.
Total CPU capacity of each host: the spe: Total CPU capacity of each host: the speed of all its CPU cores added together, in MHz or GHz.
Total bytes in the NetFlow records this: Total bytes in the NetFlow records this device exported for flows that started in the selected range. If the device samples traffic, this is the sampled amount; it is not scaled up.
Total data this container has received o: Total data this container has received over the network since it last started, at its latest reading. It is a running total, not a current speed; for a container on several networks it may count only one of them.
Total data this container has sent over: Total data this container has sent over the network since it last started, at its latest reading. It is a running total, not a current speed; for a container on several networks it may count only one of them.
Total memory in use on all nodes over th: Total memory in use on all nodes over the selected range, in bytes. The Memory tile above shows the same usage as a percentage of the nodes' combined memory.
Total packets in the NetFlow records thi: Total packets in the NetFlow records this device exported for flows that started in the selected range, counted the same way as Total Traffic.
Total restarts across this pod's contain: Total restarts across this pod's containers, not counting init containers. A number that keeps rising usually means a container is crashing or failing its liveness check.
Total size of this datastore, worked out: Total size of this datastore, worked out as used space plus free space from the latest report.
Total spend minus idle capacity, across: Total spend minus idle capacity, across all clusters. Cost an engine reports as unallocated is counted here rather than as idle.
Unhealthy if a clustered host is in main: Unhealthy if a clustered host is in maintenance mode or not responding, a datastore is at least 90% full, or a VM is swapped to disk; Degraded if a datastore is at least 80% full, a VM is ballooned or above 10% CPU Ready, or hosts are powered off. Unknown while the agent is disconnected.
Unhealthy if a node is offline or a high: Unhealthy if a node is offline or a high-availability (HA) resource is in error or fence; Degraded if a storage volume is over 85% full, a start-on-boot guest is stopped, a guest is in no backup job or replication fails. Unknown if the agent is disconnected.
Units are unit-level sites such as store: Units 是單元層級站點，例如門市；任何未運作的單元，即使尚無資料，也算作停機。Uptime 涵蓋 30 天，「今天」為最近 24 小時，不含維護。裝置包括其下的每個站點。
Up for each interval of the selected ran: Up for each interval of the selected range in which this host's agent sent metrics, Down if it sent none; a lone missed minute between Up minutes counts as Up. The uptime badge is the share of Up intervals, leaving out recent ones still waiting for data.
Up if OneUptime received metrics from th: Up if OneUptime received metrics from this host in that interval, Down if nothing arrived; the uptime badge is the share of intervals that were up. The newest interval is not judged until its data can arrive, and one missed minute between up ones counts as up.
Up means enabled with a working link, Do: Up means enabled with a working link, Down means enabled with no link, and Disabled means an administrator switched the port off, as of the last successful SNMP walk.
Up means the OSD's daemon is running and: Up means the OSD's daemon is running and answering the cluster; Down means it is not. Taken from the latest data Ceph reported for the OSD.
Up means this OSD's daemon is running an: Up means this OSD's daemon is running and responding to the cluster; Down means it has stopped or cannot be reached. From the most recent data the cluster sent.
Up to five containers using the most CPU: Up to five containers using the most CPU, ranked by each one's average in its latest interval in the last 5 minutes of the selected range (on ranges over 12 hours, often anywhere in it). 100% is one full CPU core.
Up to five containers with the highest m: Up to five containers with the highest memory percentage - of their memory limit, or of host memory if none - ranked by each one's average in its latest interval in the last 5 minutes of the selected range (on ranges over 12 hours, often anywhere in it).
Up to five tasks or instances seen in th: Up to five tasks or instances seen in the last 15 minutes, ordered by their latest CPU reading, highest first, with each one's latest memory in use; it ignores the selected time range. Ones that have not reported CPU show a dash and may be listed first.
Up to six ports: down ones first, then p: Up to six ports: down ones first, then ports with errors, then the busiest. Each row shows inbound / outbound Mbps and utilization (the busier direction as a share of link speed), averaged between the last two SNMP walks.
Upload requests the server turned away,: Upload requests the server turned away, by reason. Each request counts once even when it carried several chunks. The counts are kept per UTC day and this adds today to all of yesterday, so it covers between 24 and 48 hours, not exactly the last 24.
Used share of the host's largest filesys: Used share of the host's largest filesystem, the same mount as the Filesystem tile, in each interval of the selected range. Reserved space counts toward the total.
Used space added up across all datastore: Used space added up across all datastores in each interval of the selected range, in bytes.
Used space added up across all storage v: Used space added up across all storage volumes over the selected range. Storage that several nodes share, such as NFS or Ceph, is counted once for each node that reports it, so this total can be higher than the space really used.
Used space as a share of this datastore': Used space as a share of this datastore's capacity, from the latest report. Flagged amber from 80% and red from 90%, the levels that mark the vCenter Degraded and Unhealthy.
Used space as a share of this mount's to: Used space as a share of this mount's total size, reserved space included, averaged over the selected range. The bar turns amber at 75% and red at 90%.
Used space as a share of this volume's t: Used space as a share of this volume's total size, at its latest report. Above 85% the cluster is marked Degraded.
Used space divided by used plus free spa: Used space divided by used plus free space on each node's disk, averaged across nodes over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). One nearly full node can hide behind emptier ones.
Used space on the host's largest filesys: Used space on the host's largest filesystem, as a share of its total size with reserved space included. Averaged over the whole selected range, not the last 5 minutes; the Filesystems table lists every mount.
VM templates in the cluster: master copi: VM templates in the cluster: master copies used to create new VMs, which are never powered on.
VM templates in this cluster: master cop: VM templates in this cluster: master copies used to create new VMs. Templates are never powered on, so they use no CPU or memory.
Viewing in {{viewZone}}. This schedule h: 正在以 {{viewZone}} 檢視。此排程未設定時區，因此按伺服器本地時間呼叫。
Viewing in {{viewZone}}. This schedule i: 正在以 {{viewZone}} 檢視。此排程按 {{scheduleZone}} 設定和呼叫，下面的時間僅供參考。
Visitor sessions with a Session Replay r: Visitor sessions with a Session Replay recording in the selected range. Counting stops at 50, so "50+" means there are more - open Session Replay to see them all.
Waiting for the first progress update: 正在等待第一次進度更新
Warm copies of this function's runtime (: Warm copies of this function's runtime (faas.instance) on record, whatever the selected range. One that stops reporting is dropped about 15 minutes later by default while the function keeps reporting; an idle function keeps its last list.
We could not check what this deletes: {{: We could not check what this deletes: {{error}} Deleting a notification method also deletes every notification rule that uses it.
We could not confirm whether a reminder: 無法確認提醒是否已送達 {{name}}。{{reason}}再次傳送前，請先與 {{firstName}} 確認。
We could not match this rule to your not: We could not match this rule to your notification rules, so we cannot tell what deleting it leaves uncovered.
We could not read who is in {{group}}, s: 無法讀取 {{group}} 的成員，因此尚未檢查該排程中的任何人。
無法讀取 {{group}} 的成員，因此尚未檢查該團隊中的任何人。
What kind of unit this is, taken from th: What kind of unit this is, taken from the end of its name, for example Service for a background program or Timer for a scheduled job.
What the broker reports about this queue: 代理程式回報的此佇列資訊：積壓、消費者延遲、死信和訊息存留時間。
What this autoscaler watches and the lev: What this autoscaler watches and the level it aims for. For example, cpu (Utilization: 70) keeps average CPU near 70% of the pods' CPU requests; custom, external and per-container targets show only their type name.
What this cluster spent in the selected: What this cluster spent in the selected range on node capacity that no workload requested or used.
What this cluster spent on workloads in: What this cluster spent on workloads in the selected range: its total cost minus idle capacity.
What this container is doing right now:: What this container is doing right now: running, waiting (for example pulling its image or backing off after a crash) or terminated (it finished or was stopped).

Whether each device answered its most re: Whether each device answered its most recent check, the probe's ping or SNMP walk. A monitor-backed device is Down only when its bound monitor reports it offline and Up otherwise, and Pending means no result yet.

Whether the OneUptime Proxmox agent is s: Whether the OneUptime Proxmox agent is sending data for this cluster. It switches to Disconnected 15 to 20 minutes after data stops arriving, and the numbers on this page may then be out of date.
Whether the OneUptime VMware agent is se: Whether the OneUptime VMware agent is sending data for this vCenter; it switches to Disconnected about 15 to 20 minutes after data stops arriving. While it is disconnected the numbers on this page stop updating and may be out of date.
Whether the cluster's agent sent metrics: Whether the cluster's agent sent metrics (a heartbeat) in each interval: Up if any arrived, Down if none did; a lone missed minute between Up ones counts as Up. The badge is the share of Up intervals, leaving out the newest ones still waiting for data.
Whether the replay policy lets recorders: Whether the replay policy lets recorders run, and the share of sessions recorded from their first moment. Write access lets the agent cancel a run: 寫入權限讓代理程式能夠取消執行中的查詢，並一次結束一個工作階段——以其登入帳號的授權所允許的範圍為限，這是硬性上限。OneUptime 仍會守住底線：它從不執行任意 SQL，從不變更設定、結構描述、資料、使用者或複寫，也從不結束自己的工作階段。
Write access lets the agent force-update: 寫入權限讓代理程式能夠透過管理節點的 Docker 通訊端，對服務執行強制更新（重新啟動）、回復、擴縮與更新，以及變更節點的可用性——這相當於該節點上的 root 權限，因此指令策略、寫入開關與寫入目標是唯一的限制。OneUptime 仍會守住底線：它從不建立或移除服務或堆疊，從不觸及 secret 或 config，清空節點一律等待人工核准，而且設定 ONEUPTIME_AI_WRITE_TARGETS 後，它只會觸及其中列出的服務與節點。
Write access lets the agent mark OSDs in: 寫入權限讓代理程式能夠將 OSD 標記為 in、out 或 down，設定及取消叢集旗標，調整 OSD 權重，對 PG 執行 scrub 及修復，對 mgr 進行容錯移轉，以及重新啟動、停止與啟動常駐程式——以其 keyring 的 caps 所允許的範圍為限，這是硬性上限。OneUptime 仍會守住底線：它從不清除（purge）或銷毀 OSD，從不刪除或重新設定儲存池，從不觸及 auth 或 config-key，暫停用戶端 I/O 一律等待人工核准，而且設定 ONEUPTIME_AI_WRITE_TARGETS 後，它只會觸及其中列出的目標。
Write access lets the agent power VMs on: 寫入權限讓代理程式能夠對虛擬機器執行開機、關機、重設、暫停與重新開機，以及讓主機結束維護模式——以其 vSphere 角色所允許的範圍為限，這是硬性上限。OneUptime 仍會守住底線：它從不銷毀、建立、重新設定虛擬機器或為其建立快照，移轉虛擬機器或進入維護模式一律等待人工核准，而且設定 ONEUPTIME_AI_WRITE_TARGETS 後，它只會觸及其中列出的虛擬機器與主機。
Write access lets the agent restart, sta: 寫入權限讓代理程式能夠在此主機上重新啟動、啟動、重新載入、停止及重設 systemd 單元，清理 journal 日誌，以及向處理程序傳送訊號——它以特權模式在主機的命名空間中執行，因此指令策略、寫入開關與寫入目標是唯一的限制。OneUptime 仍會守住底線：它從不啟用、遮蔽（mask）或編輯單元，從不重新開機或關機，變更受保護的單元（sshd、systemd-*、dbus、networking、docker 等）及終止處理程序一律等待人工核准，而且設定 ONEUPTIME_AI_WRITE_TARGETS 後，它只會觸及其中列出的單元。

寫入權限讓代理程式能夠透過 Docker 通訊端重新啟動、啟動、停止、強制終止、暫停及更新（記憶體、CPU、重新啟動策略）容器——這相當於此主機上的 root 權限，因此指令策略、寫入開關與寫入目標是唯一的限制。OneUptime 仍會守住底線：它從不執行 exec、run、rm 或 prune，從不變更代理程式本身或其旁邊的收集器，而且設定 ONEUPTIME_AI_WRITE_TARGETS 後，只會觸及其中列出的容器。
